description.narrative:
PACJAs initiativ ”Galvanizing and Unifying African Voices for Resilient Development in a Multipolar World” (GUARD-AFRICA PLUS 2025–2027) ligger i linje med Sidas strategiska prioriteringar för klimatanpassning och hållbar utveckling i Afrika. Det bidrar direkt till målen i Sveriges regionala strategi för utvecklingssamarbete i Afrika.
GUARD-AFRICA PLUS bygger vidare på resultaten från fasen 2022–2024 och syftar till att öka insatserna för lokalt ledd anpassning (LLA), klimaträttvisa och kapacitetsuppbyggnad för icke-statliga aktörer. Initiativet kommer att genomföras i 12 afrikanska länder, öka finansieringen för samhällsdrivna klimatåtgärder och utvidga LLA Community of Practice. Dessa insatser syftar till att förstärka en enad afrikansk röst i den globala klimatdebatten.
Projektet kommer att följa fem strategiska vägar för att ta itu med kritiska utmaningar relaterade till klimatförändringar och hållbar utveckling i Afrika och globalt. De fem strategiska vägarna omfattar: motståndskraftiga försörjningssystem, kapacitetsuppbyggnad för intressenter, mobilisering av klimatfinansiering, rättvis omställning och resursrättigheter samt stärkande av PACJA:s institutionella kapacitet.
Den totala budgeten för GUARD-AFRICA PLUS är 138 miljoner kronor, varav 50 miljoner kronor tillhandahålls av Sida.
PACJA är ett panafrikanskt konsortium som består av över 2 000 organisationer i 54 länder, däribland gräsrots- och samhällsbaserade grupper, trossamfund, icke-statliga organisationer, stiftelser, fonder, ursprungsbefolkningar, jordbrukare och pastoralistgrupper.

PACJA’s “Galvanizing and Unifying African Voices for Resilient Development in a Multipolar World” (GUARD-AFRICA PLUS 2025–2027) initiative aligns closely with Sida’s strategic priorities on climate resilience and sustainable development in Africa. It directly contributes to the objectives outlined in Sweden’s regional strategy for development cooperation in Africa. Building on the achievements of the 2022–2024 phase, GUARD-AFRICA PLUS aims to scale up efforts in locally led adaptation (LLA), climate justice advocacy, and capacity building for non-state actors. It will operate across 12 African countries, increasing funding for community-driven climate action and expanding the LLA Community of Practice. These efforts aim to amplify a unified African voice in global climate discourse. The project will follow five strategic pathways to address critical challenges related to climate change and sustainable development in Africa and globally. The five strategic pathways include: Resilient Livelihood Systems; Capacity Building for Stakeholders; Climate Finance Mobilization; Just Transition & Resource Rights and Strengthening PACJA’s Institutional Capacity. The total budget for GUARD-AFRICA PLUS is 138 million SEK, with 50 million SEK provided by Sida. PACJA is a pan-African consortium comprising over 2,000 organizations across 54 countries, including grassroots and community-based groups, faith-based organizations, NGOs, trusts, foundations, indigenous communities, farmers, and pastoralist groups.

The objective of the intervention in the GUARD-Plus Project is to harness the collective power of African non-state actors to influence governments and other duty bearers in securing environmental and climate justice.
The intervention aims to address critical challenges related to climate change and sustainable development by implementing five key pathways:
1. Resilient Livelihood Systems for Communities at the Frontline of Climate Crisis Enhancing the resilience of vulnerable populations to adapt to changing environmental conditions and reduce susceptibility to climate-related risks.
2. Enhanced Capacity of Stakeholders to Engage in Implementation of Paris Agreement Instruments Strengthening knowledge and skills of key actors to foster more effective climate policies and actions.
3. Unlocking Climate Finance for Climate Action Addressing the inadequacy and inaccessibility of climate finance, and advocating for increased and simplified access to climate funds.
4. Ensuring African Peoples' Fair Share, Rights, and Dignity in the Just Transition Advocating for fair and inclusive policies that safeguard communities and promote responsible resource management.
5. Enhancing the Capacity of PACJA Organs, National Platforms, and Sector-Based Initiatives Strengthening collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and strategic partnerships to catalyze action for resilient development across Africa.
By the end of the intervention, the project aims to ensure stronger policy advocacy, enhanced stakeholder engagement, improved access to climate finance, and increased resilience for frontline communities in the face of climate change.
